review_scope: development-only expansion; no train/validation/test assignment and no model use
method: Reviewed the opening 45 and closing 20 rendered lines of all 15 chapters.
Searched every rendered file for YAML boundaries, Carpentries directive delimiters, code fences, Liquid expressions, Markdown link remnants and HTML tags.
Inspected all three paragraph matches reported at five-word-shingle Jaccard >= 0.80.
Compared retained attribution bytes, pinned repository/path/commit metadata and license evidence hashes against the registry and report.

paragraph_match_interpretation: One exact 40-word CSV data example is shared by two shell chapters.
One exact 37-word NumPy output and one 36/37-word formatting variant appear across two Python chapters.
The matches are retained as legitimate instructional examples and isolated by the shared Carpentries split group.
editorial_notes: Prose, exercises, solutions, command examples and code output are retained.
Image links are represented by available alternative text; image files are not ingested.
Markdown demonstration text inside lesson examples can intentionally remain because it is lesson content rather than unresolved source markup.
source_limitations: All chapters belong to one organizational/source family despite coming from five repositories.
The wave is technical and English-only and contributes 241149 characters, so it does not satisfy the planned corpus size or independent-group diversity.
The renderer is reviewed for this Carpentries Markdown format only.

decision: Accept as a development-only first expansion wave. Keep all documents in source-family:the-carpentries, exclude them from the future untouched test, and acquire unrelated licensed families before freezing splits.
